contract: spec/tc1/EFFECTS.md (draft 9: slices H1 and H2, the remote effect class with its must-use rule, remote perform, section 12, and peers written in the language with the store effects, section 12.12)
aggregation: As the TC0-A gate (TC0-GATE, 02 §14): any required row FAIL -> FAIL; else any BLOCKED -> BLOCKED; else any UNKNOWN -> UNKNOWN; else PASS. A defect killed on no program is FAIL; a crash is never a kill. An evaluator error or a check that does not report is UNKNOWN. Every row's reasons are reported whatever the aggregate. Optional rows never satisfy a required row.

rows.acceptance: Clean worktree at a committed HEAD; every later row binds to it. A dirty tree is UNKNOWN (evidence not source-bound).

The Shen/JIT executable and library directory the gate runs on resolve to the flake's shen-jit output, and the Erlang/OTP the supervisor would be built and run with (harness/find-erlang.sh) resolves to the flake's erlang output. No nix, no such flake output, or no Erlang/OTP at all: BLOCKED. Another Shen/JIT or another Erlang/OTP: UNKNOWN.
node --test tests/tc0/*.test.mjs tests/tc1/*.test.mjs: no failures. Any skipped test is UNKNOWN.

TC0-A gate rows still pass: the TC0-A evaluator (harness/gate.shen, manifest spec/tc0/tc0-a-requirements.json) is run as a prerequisite in this run, on the same HEAD, and its verdict is this row's status. Its rows are not re-implemented here. No report, another schema or another HEAD: UNKNOWN. Its waivers are reported as waivers of this gate.

harness/tc1-handlers.shen. On every TC1 hand fixture (tail-resumptive handlers and explicit one-shot resumptions) the model and the sandboxed implementation agree and satisfy the handwritten expectations, and every injected handler defect is detected on some fixture.

harness/tc1-exhaustive.shen: every program of grammar H (tools/tc1/handler-enumerate.mjs) with at most 7 nodes, 12,693 programs, agrees with the model run in the harness (every step, and the outcome), with the implementation sandboxed. A truncated scope, or a program count other than 12,693 (the number the evaluator holds, which the harness also derives from the grammar), is UNKNOWN.

The injected defect forgotten_resume (a clause return that discards the suspended segment) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.

The injected defect double_resume (a clause return that restores the suspended segment twice) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.

The injected defect outermost_handler (a perform that selects the outermost matching handler) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.

The injected defect dynamic_clause_environment (a clause run in the bindings of the perform site) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.

The injected defect resume_returns_argument (a resume that yields its argument instead of the handled body's result) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.

The injected defect shallow_resume (a resumed segment that comes back without its handler) is killed (completed, trace differs from the model's) on at least one exhaustive program; crashes are never kills. No exhaustive report in this run: UNKNOWN.
harness/solo5-pure-call.shen on the TC1 hand fixtures with the TC0-A hand cases. The Solo5 guest agrees with the model on every step and both guest defects are detected. Solo5 not built: BLOCKED.

harness/solo5-pure-call.shen on every program of grammar H with at most 7 nodes, with the TC0-A hand cases. The Solo5 guest agrees with the model on every step and both guest defects are detected. A batch whose handler family does not hold 12,693 programs, or a comparison that did not cover the whole batch, is UNKNOWN. Solo5 not built: BLOCKED.

harness/tc1-random.shen: 20,000 handler programs generated in Shen (harness/tc1-generate.shen: main bodies of at most 40 nodes, three effects, both clause forms) from 20 fixed seeds, 1,000 programs per seed. The validator accepts every one; one rejection, or a node count that differs from the generator's, is FAIL. Every program agrees with the model run in the harness, with the implementation sandboxed: both complete with the same steps and outcome, or both reach the step bound of 1,000 with the same steps up to it. A family in which no program performs, none resumes, none discontinues or none abandons a suspended segment is FAIL. Another number of programs, or no report: UNKNOWN.

harness/solo5-pure-call.shen on the programs the random-family row wrote in this run, one Solo5 guest image per seed, built with the same step bound. The guest agrees with the model on every step of every program and both guest defects are detected in every batch. No passing random-family row in this run, a batch that did not report, or batches that are not this run's 20,000 programs and steps: UNKNOWN. Solo5 not built: BLOCKED.

The random-family row's own check, on one seed of 1,000 programs, with each of the six injected defects switched on in the implementation in turn: it is FAIL every time, and PASS on the same programs with no defect. A control that passes with a defect, or fails without one, is FAIL.

harness/tc1-reduce.shen: for each of the six injected defects, a generated program on which it fails is found (model and undefective implementation agree; the defective implementation completes with a different trace; a crash or a run that reaches the step bound is not a failure) and its choice list is shrunk, every candidate being regenerated and so valid. The failure holds on every shrunk program and none is larger than its original. A defect with no failing generated program, or a disagreement between the model and the undefective implementation, is FAIL.

harness/tc1-replay.shen, in a fresh process, on the failures the random-reduction row recorded in this run: for each of the six defects the original and the shrunk choice lists regenerate programs of the recorded sizes (the shrunk one exactly the recorded program), the model and the undefective implementation agree on both, and the defective implementation completes with a different trace on both, on the shrunk program first differing from the model at the recorded step. No reduction in this run: UNKNOWN.

harness/tc1-remote.shen, as harness/run-tc1-remote.sh runs it. Model-level bounded exploration: no image and no supervisor is run. The model's peers are programs: the source files examples/remote/ledger-peer.fen and examples/remote/rates-peer.fen (and tests/remote/peers/pots.fen, in hand schedules), elaborated by the frontend and admitted by the artifact validator, and run by the model's handler machine with the store effects (models/tc1/remote-tc1-peer.shen), so that what acting does is the program's. The whole reachable state graph of 10 small systems of models/tc1/remote-system.shen is explored, one of them performing a read-only operation beside one that changes state and one with a peer that has no durable store, and every property of spec/tc1/EFFECTS.md section 12.8 holds in every state and on every step; every step kind of the model is taken; each of the 17 model mutants is killed on the property it is aimed at (an error is never a kill); the 23 hand schedules pass; and the negative control, the same checker with the non-idempotent peer in place of the model, run first, failed with a failure exit status. Any of these not so: FAIL. No report, or other numbers of systems, mutants or hand schedules: UNKNOWN.

harness/tc1-remote-run.shen, as harness/run-tc1-remote-run.sh runs it. Observed histories on spt accepted by the model: the Erlang/OTP supervisor (supervisor/) with a caller image and a peer image as Solo5 guests on the spt tender, run under 31 hand schedules, 50 seeded schedules and 5 free-running runs, of two systems. In the ledger system (examples/remote/ledger-system.json) the caller image's program is the source file examples/remote/ledger-caller.fen and the peer image's is examples/remote/ledger-peer.fen, a program that serves the remote effect and reaches the peer's durable store through the store effects; both are elaborated by the frontend (frontend/), to artifacts of schema tc1-handler-demo/3 and tc1-handler-demo/4, both include one declarations file, and the peer image's runtime commits each request's writes with its reply record in one step. In the rates system (examples/remote/rates-system.json) the caller only reads and the peer image has no durable store; 2 of the hand schedules, 10 of the seeded ones and 1 free-running run are of it. What each image declares of itself, a digest of each remote effect's signature included, is derived by the build from its own program and from the system manifest, which states the members, their programs, the declared connections and the binding of each remote effect of a caller to a member, and which the supervisor checks at assembly; five of the hand schedules are refusals at assembly, of a remote effect the manifest binds to no member, of one bound to a name that is no member, of one bound to a member the manifest declares no connection to, of a peer image with no durable store that serves an operation which is not read-only, and of a peer image whose digest of the effect's signature is not the caller's. Two hand schedules place a kill inside the peer's commit, and the supervisor's report must show that every record of the commit was written and none counted when the image was killed. Every recorded run is accepted: each recorded step is enabled in the model and the supervisor's enabled steps are the model's, the properties of section 12.8 hold on the replay, and the images' consoles and the peer's store file, cell by cell and record by record, are what the model says, and the run had one relay process more than the supervisor restarts it recorded; every scheduled run is made twice with equal recordings; every step kind of the model occurs; each of the 12 defect switches of the real system is killed (an error is never a kill); and the negative control, the non-idempotent peer image judged as if it were the peer, run first, failed with a failure exit status. Any of these not so: FAIL. Erlang/OTP not available, or the images cannot be built (Solo5 not built at the pinned commit, or the frontend does not elaborate a source): BLOCKED. A supervisor that does not compile, no report, other numbers of schedules or defects, or another tender: UNKNOWN. Four free-running runs depend on the wall clock.

harness/tc1-peer-requests.shen, as harness/run-tc1-peer-requests.sh runs it. Agreement of three implementations on listed cases: for 22 hand cases and 400 generated cases from one fixed seed, each a peer program (examples/remote/ledger-peer.fen, examples/remote/rates-peer.fen or tests/remote/peers/pots.fen), one of the operations it serves, a request input and a store, the Shen model, the JavaScript machine and the C machine in a Solo5 guest on the spt tender, which uses the store code of the peer image, agree on the whole run: every machine step, every store perform with its value, how the run ended and the writes it would commit. The model gives the expected outcome and writes of every hand case, and the defect of a read that does not see its own request's writes is detected in the JavaScript and in the C store code. Any of these not so: FAIL. The cases or the guest cannot be built (Solo5 not built at the pinned commit, or the frontend does not elaborate a peer program): BLOCKED. No report, other numbers of cases, or another tender: UNKNOWN. The commit, the reply record, replay and conflict are not exercised by this row: they are the remote-run row's.

Optional. harness/tc1-coverage.shen: every reference step kind of spec/tc1/EFFECTS.md section 6 (fifteen kinds from its thirteen rows) is exercised by this run's agreeing hand or exhaustive traces. An uncovered kind is UNKNOWN and is listed; a step classified under a kind the table does not have is FAIL. A measure of the traces, not of compiled code.

review: campaigns/tc1/TC1_GATE_REGISTRATION.md. Owner-accepted on 2026-11-15 by instruction in conversation, not by line review of the manifest, the evaluator or the checks; the status says owner-accepted, not owner-reviewed, for that reason. Registered as the check tc1-qualification in .pi/fenrir-workflow.json. Amended on 2026-11-16 (Amendment 1 of that record: the scope of the rows remote-model and remote-run, after the owner's rulings on questions 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 of EFFECTS.md section 12.10), again by instruction in conversation and not by line review. Amended on 2026-11-16 a second time (Amendment 2 of that record: the remote effect class and read-only operations, after the owner's rulings on questions 7 and 9 of EFFECTS.md section 12.10; the caller image is built from a source file through the frontend), in the same way. Amended on 2026-11-16 a third time (Amendment 3 of that record: the must-use rule for remote outcomes and the binding of remote effects in the system manifest, after the owner's rulings on questions 11, 12, 14 and 16 of EFFECTS.md section 12.10), in the same way. Amended on 2026-11-16 a fourth time (Amendment 4 of that record: peers written in the language, with the store effects, per-request transactions and a commit that is atomic at record granularity; read-only checked on the peer's program; shared declarations by include and a signature digest checked at assembly; and a third remote row, remote-peer, after the owner's rulings on questions 13 and 15 of EFFECTS.md section 12.10), in the same way.
model: models/tc1/handler-machine.shen with models/tc0/i64.shen, and for the remote rows models/tc1/remote-system.shen with models/tc1/remote-tc1-caller.shen and models/tc1/remote-tc1-peer.shen, run in-process by the Shen harness on the flake-pinned Shen/JIT
not_covered: Strict replay of whole runs against recorded tapes (the reduced-replay row re-runs and re-compares; it does not replay a tape), a versioned and hashed transition catalog for the handler steps (the optional coverage row measures against the table in EFFECTS.md section 6), and any soundness proof of the typing or one-shot rules. Grammar H has one-operation effects with I64 operation types only, no closures, and programs of at most 7 nodes. The generated family is a sample, not a scope: 20,000 programs of at most 40 nodes from fixed seeds, with three effects (one of two operations, one of them returning Bool), no closures, datatypes, tuples or bytes, no Unit-typed operations, and no handle of a type other than I64; its reduction shrinks to a small failing program, not to a proven smallest one. The guest is compared with the model on the generated family, not with the six implementation defects. Remote perform: the model row explores 10 small systems under budgets of crash, duplicate and supervisor-restart steps, and the checker reads history variables the model's own steps maintain; two of its thirteen properties, commit-atomic and reads-see-own-writes, are read for the ledger peer only, from what its program means, and read-reply-from-state uses that a peer's answer never decreases. The run row is two two-member systems and a few dozen recorded histories on the spt tender, with block-device mailboxes as the transport, I64 arguments, replies of a status and an I64, and a supervisor whose event log is its own account. A peer's commit is atomic if one 512-byte block write is atomic and a write that returned survives the death of the image: neither is tested, no torn block and no lost write is injected, and the kill inside a commit is placed at one point of it, with the image's cooperation. The store's log is never compacted. A peer's program that traps is exercised in the model's hand schedules and in the remote-peer row, not on the real system, where the supervisor cannot know beforehand that acting will commit nothing. The remote-peer row compares single requests on listed cases; it has no commit, no reply record, no replay and no conflict. A peer does not call onward: a remote perform in a program that serves is rejected. The typing of the remote effect class, its must-use rule included (a remote perform only as the scrutinee of a match, the outcome type written nowhere), and the rule that the implementation of a read-only operation has no StoreWrite in its effect set, are checked by the validator and the frontend on unit and frontend tests, not proved. The signature digest covers an effect's operation names, types and read-only markers, not the definition of a datatype a type names, and nothing ties an image file to the build that made it. The supervisor's refusals about a binding are exercised by three hand schedules, its refusal of a differing signature by one, and its treatment of a malformed manifest by none; the frontend itself is exercised by this gate only as far as elaborating the programs of the two systems and the test peers; its own tests (frontend/test.sh) are not a row. A supervisor restart is covered only as the one step of section 12.7: in the run row the relay process is killed and started again between steps while the guests run, and what the contract says survives is kept by another process of the same Erlang VM, not durably; a restart at any other instant, and the loss of the whole VM, are not. No hvt run, no network transport, no liveness, no proof. See spec/tc1/EFFECTS.md sections 12.9, 12.11 and 12.12.
